source.name: Synthetic demo
source.attribution: Random deals with real double-dummy analysis; field results and commentary are made up by scripts/make_sample_game.py --demo. Not real results from any game.

boards.commentary:
Made-up commentary for the demo, not real expert analysis.

North–South hold 25 high-card points to East–West's 15.
Double dummy, par is +140 for North–South: 2♥ by North or 2♥ by South.
118 of the 293 tables (40%) bid 2♥.
The most common result was 2♥ by North, +1 (51 tables).
A part-score battle: neither side has a game, so the fight is over the 2- and 3-level. Compete to the level of your fit (eight trumps, the 2-level; nine, the 3-level).

Made-up commentary for the demo, not real expert analysis.

North–South hold 5 high-card points to East–West's 35.
Double dummy, par is −2220 for North–South: 7NT by East or 7NT by West.
150 of the 249 tables (60%) bid 7NT.
The most common result was 7NT by East, made (79 tables).
With this many points between them, the question isn't whether to bid a slam but which one: count your top tricks before choosing between a small slam and a grand slam.
